tasks.short: Survey natural features and structures, including underground.

steps.what: Conduct surveys of natural features and structures.
Note what was not found underground or underwater.
Store the located points from this survey.

tasks.design: Conducting the survey stays outdoors, with distance-measuring equipment and other instruments. Natural features and structures on the surface, underground and underwater are located by the technician. {OPS_SYSTEM} stores the points and the gaps. A model does not place a feature that was not observed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Locations lived in the field book and were typed into the map later.
tasks.enabler_now: A point id and a found-or-not flag are fields. Seeing the feature is not.
tasks.still_hard: A structure that is buried, or a bank that the instrument cannot see, stays a search.
tasks.human_edge: The technician can tell a culvert from a shadow and knows when the shot is unsafe.
tasks.altitude: The point log takes less retyping. The survey and the note of what was not found stay.

evidence.claim: Storing a point id is a record. Locating a feature with an instrument is not.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the technician conducts the survey and notes gaps. Calculating coordinates is a different task. The party chief owns the job.

Structured input: point id, feature type, surface or underground or underwater, coordinates if the collector stored them. Producer is the technician on the survey. A row with no point id is kept as a gap note.
Field time stays. The log does not invent a location.
unknowns: Which instruments store a point in the field?
How are underwater shots booked today?
research_questions: How often is an underground feature omitted from the later map?

already_counted.description: Conducting the survey is already the remaining time on that step.

incremental.description: Retire point rows for surveys that closed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the collector stores nothing, the survey is unchanged and the log is typed once afterwards. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare topographic and contour maps from survey notes.

steps.what: Prepare topographic maps from the survey notes.
Draft contour lines only from stored points.

loop.input: point ids and heights already stored for this survey
loop.output: contour lines that cite only those point ids
loop.check: every vertex must be a stored point; else discard
loop.stop: one draft; a gap in the points is left blank
loop.why_not_simpler: which site features belong on the sheet is the decision

steps.what: Accept site features, charts and drawings.

tasks.design: The technician prepares the topographic sheet from the survey notes, charts and drawings. Contour lines may be drafted only from points already stored on {DATA_PLATFORM}. The technician accepts the site features. {OPS_SYSTEM} files that sheet. A contour is not invented where the notes have no point.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contours were drawn by hand from the book, and a wrong height was copied onto the sheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Points with heights can draw a first contour. Which features the sheet includes cannot.
tasks.still_hard: A note that disagrees with a height, or a feature the points do not show, stays a correction.
tasks.human_edge: The technician knows which breakline the points have smoothed away.
tasks.altitude: Redrawing every contour from scratch takes less time. Choosing features and accepting the sheet stay.

reach.task: Use the filed sheet, not the draft

evidence.claim: A contour through stored heights is a draft. The source pack names survey software that draws from points. Accepting the sheet is the pattern's human step, not a measured case here.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the technician prepares and accepts the map. Publishing it to a client is a different task if someone else signs the issue.
Structured input: point id, height, survey id. Producer is the point log. A draft vertex with no point id is discarded.
Acceptance is remaining time. The file does not add a feature the technician removed.
unknowns: Are heights stored on the same points as the notes?
research_questions: How often is a contour redrawn because a height was typed wrong?

already_counted.description: Preparing the sheet from the notes is already the remaining time on that step.

incremental.description: Retire draft contours when the survey points change.

approvals.approved_version: sheet the technician accepted for that survey

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If points are not stored, there is no contour draft and the technician still prepares the sheet from the notes. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise workers who survey, plot and draft.

steps.what: Coordinate activities of workers engaged in surveying.
Supervise workers surveying, plotting or drafting maps.
Log finished blueprints, photostats and photographs.

tasks.design: Coordinating and supervising the workers stays in person. Surveying, plotting, drafting maps, and producing blueprints, photostats and photographs are watched by the technician. {PROJECT} logs what was finished. It does not score a worker or assign the next job.
tasks.previous_blocker: The day was arranged by talking, and a finished photograph was forgotten.
tasks.enabler_now: A finished-or-not flag is a field. Whether a worker needs help is not.
tasks.still_hard: A crew that is short, or a plot that is going wrong, stays supervision.
tasks.human_edge: The technician sees who is stuck without a score.
tasks.altitude: The day log takes less chasing. Coordinating and supervising stay. Nobody is ranked.

reach.learn: Which job had no one on it

evidence.claim: A finished-item log is a list. Supervising a crew is not.
The source pack names a rule that assigning work from worker performance needs consent. This design stores no score and does not assign the next job. Other countries differ.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the technician supervises today's work. Hiring and performance reviews are different tasks.
Structured input: job id, product type (blueprint, photostat, photograph, plot), finished or not. Producer is the technician. A row with a worker score is refused.
Supervision time stays. The log is not a ranking.
unknowns: Who may move a worker between jobs?
Is a finished photograph already on the job?
research_questions: How often is the same plotting job left without a named person?

already_counted.description: Supervising the workers is already the remaining time on that step.

incremental.description: Retire day logs after the job closes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the day's jobs are only spoken, supervision is unchanged and the log is a short note. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile a stake list from engineering plans.

steps.what: Read engineering plans for the construction projects.
Compile information necessary to stake those projects.
Walk the stake positions before construction starts.

tasks.design: The technician reads the engineering plans. {DATA_PLATFORM} compiles a stake list only where coordinates already exist for that project. Walking the positions stays in the field. A plan note that has no coordinate is not given one.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stake lists were copied off the plan by hand, and a point was missed until the site walk.
tasks.enabler_now: Coordinates already stored can be listed. Reading what the plan asks to stake cannot.
tasks.still_hard: A plan revision, or a coordinate that does not match the drawing, stays a reading and a walk.
tasks.human_edge: The technician sees a plan call the coordinate list does not mention.
tasks.altitude: Copying known coordinates takes less time. Reading the plans and walking the positions stay.

reach.task: Take the stake list to site
reach.learn: Which plan call had no coordinate

evidence.claim: Listing stored coordinates is a query. Reading an engineering plan is not.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the technician compiles the list and walks it. Setting the stakes is a different task. The construction lead owns the build.

Structured input: project id, plan id, point id, coordinate. Producer is the plan store for coordinates and the technician for what must be staked. A call with no coordinate is listed as missing, not filled.
The walk stays. The list does not move a stake.
research_questions: How often does a stake list miss a call that was only on the drawing?

already_counted.description: Reading the plans is already the remaining time on that step.

incremental.description: Retire stake lists when the plan revision changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the plans have no stored coordinates, the list is empty and the technician still reads and walks. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Surveys of features, and the walk to check stakes, stay outdoors. Contours are drafted only from stored points, and the technician accepts the sheet. Supervising workers is not a ranking.
reach: The party chief sees features that were not found.
A filed map is the accepted sheet, not the contour draft.
skills_to_grow: Record a gap rather than a guessed location.
Do not score a worker in the day log.
role.ambitious_version: A buried feature is logged as not found the same day, and a worker is not assigned by a score.
